## 4. Acquisition and error costs

At each uniform preload +/-P, measure q at +/-h0*e0 and +/-h1*e1.
The four points estimate both columns of the tangent matrix by central
differences: eight vector measurements total. Maxwell reciprocity can average
the two off-diagonal estimates; inconsistency is a diagnostic, not an error
bound. Repeat measurements only reduce a declared stochastic term under
their actual dependence model; they do not remove systematic error.

If individual q-coordinate error is bounded by s_i, the open-minus-closed
central-difference entry error is at most 2*s_i/h_j. If the relevant third
derivative of q is bounded, central-difference truncation adds h_j^2/6
times that bound per preload. These budgets, load calibration and coordinate
cross-talk must fit into the supplied entry box.

For zero initial gap and affine residual center/gradient bounds rho0,rhog,
depth |r|<=R and radius a<=Amax, a sufficient ideal switching condition is

    P > rho0+Amax*rhog+max(h0, h1*(R+2*Amax/H)).                 (9)

The maximum uses the actual protocol's one-mode-at-a-time probe settings.
If combined probes occupy the whole h0/h1 rectangle, replace that maximum
by their sum; it is a different, more costly load protocol.

A finite initial aperture requires an additional acquired closure-pressure
bound; the code accepts its equivalent stress in (9). For a gap profile
proportional to sqrt(a^2-rho^2), that equivalent stress follows directly
from the uniform opening solution. Arbitrary apertures require an actual
contact calculation. Neither a geometric aspect ratio nor an average gap
alone proves (9) for arbitrary contact geometry.
This extra parameter controls switching only. A real finite-aperture void
also changes the opening operator and service SIF; preserving the disk law
requires a justified finite-aspect model-error enclosure. It is not silently
converted into a zero-thickness fracture by supplying a closure pressure.

An upper test opening intensity is

    2*sqrt(Amax/pi)*[P+rho0+(2/3)*Amax*rhog
                    +max(h0, h1*R+(4/3)*h1*Amax/H)].            (10)

This number must lie in an independently validated reversible/no-growth
load envelope, with yield, stability and cycle effects included. A fracture
toughness alone does not prove nondestructiveness. Compression also needs
its own yield/contact-damage bound. No such physical envelope is acq

# Contact-weighted compliance acquisition bridge

**Completed:** a conditional, executable map from an imperfect open/closed
compliance contrast to a bound on the largest crack's service stress
intensity, without reconstructing the crack population. **Not achieved:**
acquisition of the contact, measurement, component-model or nondestructive
load premises for a real specimen. New physical mechanism, practical method
advantage and world novelty are not established.

The result is narrower than the original preload hypothesis. Open-minus-
closed differential compliance is an existing measurement. The useful
extension constructed here retains nonzero closed-contact compliance and
turns it into an explicit radius-dependent sensitivity, rather than treating
compression as a pristine reference.

## Constructed operation

Use the peer's tension/bending convention: p=(p0,p1), stress p0+p1*r,
r=2z/H, and v(r)=(1,r). Let beta=16(1-nu²)/(3E). A circular finite disk
has the open matrix

    C_open/beta = a³ [[1,r],[r,r²+(8/15)(a/H)²]].

The positive a⁵ term is the crack's own bending extent. The peer has
corrected its physical convention and can retain this term conservatively.
I independently obtained it both by opening-displacement integration and
by integrating the primary uniform/bending energy-release rates. The
underlying source is the infinite-medium penny-crack solution of
[Nishioka et al.2008](https://doi.org/10.1299/jcst.2.34), including its
visually checked bending Eq60. This is not a finite-component correction.

Suppose every crack is open at the positive preload and its compressed
normal-contact operator obeys K>=kI, with k>0 supplied in Pa/m. A variational
projection of the ordinary resolvent identity gives the lower contrast

    (C_open-C_compressed)/beta >= h_k(a) v(r)v(r)^T,
    h_k(a)=a³ * beta*k*a/(pi+beta*k*a).

This derivation does not require rigid closure, a minimum crack size, or a
contact solve for every flaw. h_k is increasing. If an error-corrected
measured upper matrix U bounds the sum of these contact-weighted matrices,
every individual crack satisfies

    h_k(a) <= 1/[v(r)^T U^-1 v(r)].

Invert this scalar law, cap the radius geometrically, and maximize the
ordinary affine disk rim intensity over depth. `contact_certificate.py`
does this with rational interval bounds. `PRIMARY_PROOF.md` gives the
operator argument, finite-disk energy, err
